assessments.title: Persistent verifier metadata across the memory lifecycle
assessments.evidence_strength: Strong matched-control evidence within the reported agent-memory setting. MemGuard compares a verifier-only admission control against lifecycle-persistent verifier metadata under matched task order, step budget, retrieval budget and decoding settings; the verifier-only control underperforms full MemGuard in all 16 backbone-by-benchmark cells, averaged over five seeds.
assessments.scope_guard: Supports incremental value of persisting verifier-derived governance metadata beyond one-time admission in the four named benchmarks/backbones. Does not prove robustness to malicious/systematically corrupted verifiers, forged metadata, arbitrary environment drift, or all memory architectures.
assessments.replication_status: author-reported multi-seed evaluation with public code; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Terminating API routers break end-to-end command integrity
assessments.evidence_strength: Direct attack/defense evaluation supports the boundary claim: a plaintext-access terminating router can rewrite or exfiltrate agent interactions, while AEGIS moves plaintext handling into a client-attested enclave and blocks all four tested malicious-router classes, including adaptive tests against the same boundary. The source also reports a small trusted path and low local relay overhead.
assessments.scope_guard: Supports the tested router threat model and attested faithful-passthrough construction. It does not establish universal TEE/platform security, eliminate metadata side channels, or prove provider-signed provenance is the only alternative.
assessments.replication_status: author evaluation; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Read-side secret confinement and write-side effect authorization are distinct controls
assessments.evidence_strength: The common-harness results strongly support the practical value of SecureClaw's dual-boundary design across AgentDojo, AgentLeak and Agent Security Bench. However, the broader necessity claim that both boundaries are separately required is partly architectural reasoning rather than a complete factorial ablation of read-only versus write-only controls under every benchmark.
assessments.scope_guard: Do not upgrade the benchmark result into a universal confidentiality or authorization theorem. The trusted gateway/executor assumptions remain load-bearing and residual leakage is nonzero on AgentLeak.
assessments.replication_status: author common-harness evaluation; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Event-sourced hypothesis/evidence/belief lifecycle with evidence-gated belief mutation
assessments.evidence_strength: HEP provides a direct same-goal/same-tools/same-base-LLM process comparison against a planning-style agent (n=3 per condition). The planning agent spends most classified loop steps on tests with no explicit belief updates, while HEP exhibits explicit hypothesis-to-test-to-evidence-to-belief lifecycle cycling and enforces append-only hypothesis identity, evidence-gated belief changes and lifecycle thresholds.
assessments.scope_guard: Strong evidence for auditable process control and externalized belief-update behavior, not for superior final scientific correctness. Beliefs are elicited rather than statistically computed, the same agent validates much computational evidence, n is small for the matched process comparison, and the science fidelity is not independent experimental truth.
assessments.replication_status: author experiment; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Monotone Shapley worst-case completion as an exact maximum-closure problem
assessments.evidence_strength: The structural ingredients are externally well-supported: order-polytope vertices correspond to characteristic functions of filters/upper sets, and maximum-weight closure reduces to min-cut/max-flow. The worker's exact Shapley reduction is plausible and its integer-scaled implementation matched LP cross-checks to numerical precision.
assessments.scope_guard: The general mathematical ingredients are established, but this exact Shapley reduction/implementation was derived and tested worker-locally rather than independently published or externally reproduced. Complexity remains exponential in n because the Boolean lattice has 2^n vertices.
assessments.replication_status: worker-local derivation plus local LP spot checks; no independent implementation replication confirmed

assessments.title: Preregistered unseen-seed holdout for deterministic monotone-completion certification
assessments.evidence_strength: A durable preregistration froze the game, unseen seed set, budgets, thresholds and deterministic certifier before the holdout. Across 1000 unseen seeds there were zero solver failures and zero false certifications, providing meaningful confirmatory evidence that trusted monotonicity can tighten decision bounds on the fixed game.
assessments.scope_guard: Confirmatory only across unseen sampling seeds on one fixed synthetic game; not independent-game generalization, not proof of scalability, and safety is conditional on exact oracle values plus true monotonicity.
assessments.replication_status: worker-local preregistered holdout; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Exact target-null safety of the nine-split minimax selector
assessments.evidence_strength: The checkpoint supplies an explicit finite-time proof for the exact selector: selected-pair threshold crossing implies E1+E2 >= 3.6/delta, and the average of the two valid e-processes is itself an e-process under the joint target null, yielding the anytime bound 5 delta/9. This invocation independently checked the algebra and the stated delta=.05 value. A 500,000-trajectory sanity simulation is consistent with the bound but is not needed for the proof.
assessments.scope_guard: The proof is specific to the exact nine-split grid/minimax residual selector and the fixed target null, assuming both component processes are valid e-processes under that joint null. It does not imply unknown-parameter numerical confidence coverage off target or safety for arbitrary same-history alpha selectors.
assessments.replication_status: independent algebraic check in this comparator invocation plus worker simulation; no external formal proof or independent numerical replication

assessments.title: Fresh post-selection confirmation versus generic nine-pair insurance
assessments.evidence_strength: Exact persisted V3 module blobs were materialized and exercised on the stored 60-campaign synthetic family with 240 replay-prefix checks, 240 tamper rejections and zero target-log-e replay difference. Fresh-confirm consistently resolved with substantially lower mean stopping cost than uniform nine-pair insurance for the tested pilot sizes. The unmodified validator exceeded the time limit, so the full comparison used an algebraically deduplicated harness while preserving the exact alpha-independent paths; endpoint equality was checked on a subset.
assessments.scope_guard: Evidence is for one stored synthetic campaign family and stopping/replay behavior, not production latency/sample complexity. Full 60-campaign endpoint equality of the unchanged validator was not completed, and no claim is made that the same-history selector provides generic off-target numerical coverage.
assessments.replication_status: worker-local exact-blob execution with semantics-preserving deduplication; no independent external reproduction

assessments.title: Symptom-driven selective node repair with rescue-disruption accounting
assessments.evidence_strength: Repair or Resample evaluates 536 human-annotated MAS failures across three frameworks. Suspicious-Node repairs 20.15% with one selective intervention versus 3.73% Random-Node, 1.31% Last-Node and 6.90% unguided full rerun with up to three attempts. Separately, rerunning 54 previously successful source executions three times produced 85 failures in 162 attempts and at least one regression in 39/54 source cases, directly demonstrating a material disruption channel from broad rerun.
assessments.scope_guard: The 20.15% effect is for the joint package of symptom-based target selection plus evidence-conditioned guidance; the paper does not isolate either component. Selective one-intervention and full-rerun three-attempt arms are not compute-matched, so API efficiency is descriptive rather than a causal budget-normalized estimate.
assessments.replication_status: large author study on newly released SymTrace/SymFail evidence; no independent numerical replication confirmed

assessments.title: Fault-class-conditioned tool recovery under deterministic replay
assessments.evidence_strength: ToolMisuseBench provides deterministic replayable fault injection over 6,800 tasks and explicit step/call/retry budgets. In the released baseline table, schema/policy repair reaches about 0.502 timeout recovery and 0.497 schema-drift recovery versus 0 for the heuristic, while all released baselines remain at 0 success for authorization and rate-limit subsets and aggregate success stays 0.250. The public repository exposes the benchmark/evaluation pipeline.
assessments.scope_guard: This supports strong fault-class dependence in the released benchmark and simple baselines, not a theorem that authorization or rate-limit faults are intrinsically unrecoverable. The policy-aware baseline is explicitly lightweight, and exact paper numbers were not independently rerun from artifacts in this invocation.
assessments.replication_status: author-reported deterministic benchmark with public implementation; no independent numeric rerun in this invocation

assessments.title: ScienceFlow archived-state re-anchoring and exact historical-node restoration
assessments.evidence_strength: ScienceFlow's paper and public implementation provide direct evidence that ESTRA can choose archived execution anchors and restore executable workspace state, while the public tests exercise restoration of an exact archived node UID even when multiple historical nodes share the same visible stage ID. The paper reports 561 ESTRA decisions in telemetry and controlled mechanism ablations on long-horizon tasks, while the repository includes snapshot/recovery tests and a kill/resume script.
assessments.scope_guard: Supports recoverable archived-state routing and exact historical-node selection in the tested implementation. It does not establish semantic equivalence after arbitrary process death at every ESTRA phase: explicit restoration events are sparsely logged in the paper, and the reviewed tests do not constitute a full SIGKILL phase-boundary equivalence matrix.
assessments.replication_status: author benchmark/ablation plus public code/test inspection at exact commit; no independent end-to-end numerical replication

assessments.title: Proof-carrying recovery transaction across workspace, lineage, budget and evaluator cursors
assessments.evidence_strength: The design is well-motivated by a concrete implementation boundary: ScienceFlow keeps pending ESTRA intent as controller state, has strong exact-node/workspace restoration and ordinary-exception rollback tests, and ships a kill/resume script that may escalate to SIGKILL. The reviewed source does not establish a durable transaction journal that atomically binds pending action/target, workspace restore phase, lineage, evaluation consumption, budget/resource cursors and external-effect cursors across arbitrary kill points. The proposed phase-committed transaction and kill-injection equivalence test directly address that gap, but the composition itself is not implemented or experimentally validated here.
assessments.scope_guard: Evidence supports a specific missing assurance boundary and a falsifiable design/test proposal. It does not show that ScienceFlow published results were corrupted by crashes, that the proposed transaction protocol is sufficient for all external side effects, or that it improves task success under matched budget.
assessments.replication_status: derived design hypothesis grounded in public implementation inspection; no end-to-end implementation, kill-injection matrix or independent replication
